node_definition.done_when: (1) A new test, tests/test_forward_solve_clip_mode_request.py, runs two solves with different clip modes in one process and asserts that each receipt records its own mode and that each operator was built with it, independent of the global's value; it fails at the base revision (log committed). (3) The new field round-trips through the request and receipt serialisation, covered in the new test file. Run CPU gates in place on this fleet allocation with JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu and pytest --timeout 0; any test file over ten minutes goes through scripts/nova_lane/run.sh on the H200. The manifest status is one of complete, blocked or failed.
node_definition.goal: Carry the support clip mode as a field of the forward-solve request and receipt. This is the first of three nodes that retire the module global _SUPPORT_CLIP_MODE in nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py (followup f-fsapi-clip-mode-is-a-request-field on forward-solve-api). ForwardSolveRequest in nova/equilibrium/solve_request.py gains clip_mode with its policy default (chord, the current default), the solve entry points in nova/equilibrium/forward.py pass it as an explicit argument into the operator build in forward_operator.py so that a solve built from a request never reads the global, and ForwardSolveReceipt records it. The global and set_support_clip_mode remain only as the default for the roughly forty benchmarks and tests not yet migrated, which the next node migrates before the last node deletes both, so add no new reader of the global. Build on the frozen-Newton route merged at db580bec8, which also touches forward.py.
